title: Mother Jesus (Revelations 59–60)
hookLine: Julian speaks of our mother Christ, who feeds us with himself
tomorrow: after all those visions, what did Julian say they meant?

cards: A kid yells Mom from the other room before deciding what's even wrong. Some grown-ups still do it when they stub a toe. Julian of Norwich is choosing her words for Jesus.
Lord, yes. Brother, yes. Then she writes one that can still catch a reader off guard: mother.
Not Mary this time. Jesus. Our Mother Jesus, she writes, and she isn't being poetic for a line or two.
She stays with it, and she explains herself.

teach.b: First, she doesn't trade one name for another. As truly as God is our Father, she says, so truly God is our Mother. Father stays.

Mother is added. Then she works from what mothers actually do. A mother carries a child and brings it to birth; Julian says Jesus bears us into joy and endless life, and that this birth cost him the pain of the cross.

teach.h: HE BEARS US, AND FEEDS US.
teach.b: A mother feeds her child; our precious Mother, Jesus, feeds us with himself, and she means the bread of communion.
And a hurt or frightened child doesn't make a plan. It runs straight to its mother. That, Julian says, is how we're meant to run to him.

She isn't far from the Gospels: in Matthew, Jesus says, "how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings." A neighbor tradition reaches for a mother too.
In a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, sees a woman find her baby among a crowd of captives and hold it close to nurse it.
God, he says, is more merciful to his servants than this woman is to her child. Two traditions, each looking at a mother to say something about God's love.

teach.h: A NEIGHBOR: MERCY BEYOND A MOTHER'S.
teach.b: The difference is honest: the hadith says God's mercy is greater than a mother's, without calling God a mother, and in Islam Jesus is honored as a prophet.

how: Christians read Julian's Revelations of Divine Love slowly, a chapter at a time, and some churches remember her with a feast day.

o: a title Julian gave to Mary, the mother of Jesus
a nickname for the Church as every believer's mother
Julian's name for Christ, who loves us as a mother does

p: into joy, at the cost of the cross

s: Julian calls God Mother instead of Father
the skimmer's reading. as truly as God is our Father, so truly God is our Mother: she keeps both.
Jesus pictures himself as a hen gathering her chicks in Matthew
"even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings."
in the hadith, the Prophet compares God's mercy to a mother's love
God is more merciful to his servants than this woman is to her child.

games.q: your little cousin asks at dinner: is God a boy or a girl? what could you say from Julian, true to her book?
o: God is only a Father, so a boy.
Julian keeps both: Father, and truly Mother.
games.why: Julian writes that as truly as God is our Father, so truly God is our Mother. she adds a name; she doesn't trade one away.

practice: Do one small, mothering thing right now, for someone nearby or for yourself: fill a glass of water, set out tomorrow's lunch, plug in a phone that's dying.
Do it slowly, the way a good parent does the tenth chore of the day, and then sit with whoever it was for in mind.

wordCard.voice: Mother Jesus. Julian's name for Christ, who carries us, feeds us with himself, and never stops loving us when we fall.

carryVoice: Keep this: our precious mother, the one a hurt child runs to without stopping to think. Good night, or good morning.
